patch_description:
The existing program failed validation for multiple structural reasons: (1) it returned an empty list `[]` as `column_orderings`, so the evaluator could not reconstruct per-row column orders; (2) it added an "original_index" column, and in the col_merge path dropped/merged columns so output shapes were inconsistent; (3) it relied on undefined helper methods (`calculate_col_stats`, `merging_columns`) from the parent class and used complex thread/recursive logic (`column_recursion`, `recursive_reorder`) that built rows via `itertuples` attribute access — which breaks for columns with non-identifier names (e.g. 'review/profileName') and mixed types, causing silent row corruption/incorrect results; (4) `recursive_reorder` returned a DataFrame whose columns were renamed ("original_index" appended to column list), breaking identity; (5) objective was squared field lengths/adjacent rows, not serial character-Trie prefix reuse.

The fix replaces the editable block with a clean, bounded algorithm preserving the public API: serialize cells once (missing -> ""), build a small set of candidate global column orders (original order; frequency×length-ranked order; a simple conditional-partition order based on grouping by a high-repetition column), score each candidate with the exact ideal Trie reuse metric (sum of adjacent LCPs of lexicographically sorted serialized rows, computed with binary search on prefix slices for speed), pick the best, and return the permuted DataFrame (object dtype, same rows/cells) together with valid per-row column orderings. col_merge columns are placed contiguously (merged semantics preserved without altering values). No data is added, dropped, or fabricated.
